directAnswer: Pope Urban VII was Giovanni Battista Castagna, a Roman-born diplomat elected on 15 September 1590 who died of malaria just 13 days later, before he could be crowned. His is the shortest pontificate in history.

sections.h2: Giovanni Battista Castagna, Diplomat of Trent
paras: Giovanni Battista Castagna was born in Rome on 4 August 1521 to a Genoese family. Trained in law, he became archbishop of Rossano in Calabria in 1553, took part in the Council of Trent, and served as papal nuncio to Spain for several years and as governor in the Papal States.

Gregory XIII created him a cardinal in 1583. He also served the Inquisition. When the conclave met after Sixtus V's death, Castagna was elected on 15 September 1590 with Spanish backing and took the name Urban VII.

Accounts of his brief reign describe a pope concerned for Rome's poor, who ordered economies in the papal court. He is also credited with a decree forbidding tobacco use in or near churches, often cited as one of the earliest public smoking bans.

Urban VII contracted malaria and died on 27 September 1590, before his coronation. He left his considerable fortune to a Roman confraternity to provide dowries for poor young women. He is buried in Santa Maria sopra Minerva. Beyond these details, his reign was too short to leave a lasting mark.

keyFacts: Born Giovanni Battista Castagna in Rome on 4 August 1521
Archbishop of Rossano and participant at the Council of Trent
Papal nuncio to Spain; cardinal from 1583
Shortest pontificate in history; never crowned

faqs.question: Which pope had the shortest reign?
faqs.answer: Urban VII, who died of malaria 13 days after his election in September 1590, before his coronation.

faqs.question: Did Urban VII ban smoking?
faqs.answer: He is credited with forbidding tobacco use in and around churches, a decree often described as one of the first smoking bans, though details of its enforcement are scarce.
